newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch electricity use dips, supply rises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dutch electricity use dips, supply rises in 1996.

text.p: Dutch electricity use dipped slightly in 1996, but supply grew in response to rising foreign demand, the power generating umbrella group, Samenwerkende elektriciteits-produktiebedrijven (Sep), said on Friday.
Electricity consumption, as supplied by Sep, dipped 0.5 percent from 1995 to 1996, but reached a new peak on December 19 of 11,360 megawatts.
Sep production rose by 0.8 percent in 1996, largely the result of increased foreign demand and a slight reduction in imports.

Gas was again the most important energy source, accounting for 51 percent of electricity produced (49 percent in 1995). Coal made up 42 percent (1995: 45 percent) of production and nuclear power seven percent (1995: six percent).
Sep supplies 87 percent of the nation's electricity needs. The rest comes mainly from combined heat and power installations for individual companies.
